name: Are You Fired?
description: Levian works as an accountant in a large company. Levian knows how much the company has earned in each of the $$$n$$$ consecutive months — in the $$$i$$$-th month the company had income equal to $$$a_i$$$ (positive income means profit, negative income means loss, zero income means no change). Because of the general self-isolation, the first $$$\lceil \tfrac{n}{2} \rceil$$$ months income might have been completely unstable, but then everything stabilized and for the last $$$\lfloor \tfrac{n}{2} \rfloor$$$ months the income was the same . Levian decided to tell the directors $$$n-k+1$$$ numbers — the total income of the company for each $$$k$$$ consecutive months. In other words, for each $$$i$$$ between $$$1$$$ and $$$n-k+1$$$ he will say the value $$$a_i + a_{i+1} + \ldots + a_{i + k - 1}$$$. For example, if $$$a=[-1, 0, 1, 2, 2]$$$ and $$$k=3$$$ he will say the numbers $$$0, 3, 5$$$. Unfortunately, if at least one total income reported by Levian is not a profit (income $$$\le 0$$$), the directors will get angry and fire the failed accountant. Save Levian's career: find any such $$$k$$$, that for each $$$k$$$ months in a row the company had made a profit, or report that it is impossible.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 5\cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of months for which Levian must account. The second line contains $$$\lceil{\frac{n}{2}}\rceil$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_{\lceil{\frac{n}{2}}\rceil}$$$, where $$$a_i$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le a_i \le 10^9$$$) — the income of the company in the $$$i$$$-th month. Third line contains a single integer $$$x$$$ ($$$-10^9 \le x \le 10^9$$$) — income in every month from $$$\lceil{\frac{n}{2}}\rceil + 1$$$ to $$$n$$$.
output_specification: In a single line, print the appropriate integer $$$k$$$ or $$$-1$$$, if it does not exist. If there are multiple possible answers, you can print any.
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1358E — Are You Fired? [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
